title: SPE Chapter 08 — Auth

Capture runs logged-out, so /?o=Users redirects to login (demonstrates the guard). Rebuild: RESYNTH=1 bash scripts/make-episode.sh 08-Auth

scenes.narr: Chapter eight adds identity: real users, hashed passwords, logins, and roles. This is the sign-in form.
A users table stores each account with a hashed password and a role, seeded with two demo accounts to log in as.
Logging in looks the user up by email and verifies the password against the stored hash — the plain password is never compared directly.
And notice: a wrong email and a wrong password give the exact same message, so an attacker learns nothing about which one was wrong.
On success, the session id is regenerated before anything is stored — the standard defence against session fixation.
Authorisation is a single ordered enum. Whether one role satisfies another is just a numeric comparison inside a match expression.
By default, every method is public — anonymous visitors are welcome.
A plugin tightens that by overriding one method. Here the entire Users plugin is locked to admins in a single line.
This is the choke point every request passes through: anonymous visitors are sent to log in, and a signed-in but under-privileged user gets an honest 403.
So visiting the admin-only users page while logged out lands you straight on the login form.
While reading posts stays open to everyone — but the create, edit, and delete controls only appear once an admin is signed in.
When an admin creates a user, the password is hashed with the current best algorithm.
And on update, it is only re-hashed when a new password was actually supplied.
Even remember-me is done properly: a random selector with a separately hashed validator, compared in constant time and rotated on every use.
That is chapter eight: hashing, sessions, roles, and access control. Next, the finale — chapter nine builds a complete blog and CMS on this foundation.
